title: Normalized proper/open pasting on ambient pro-etale and semilinear-system categories
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes; their structure morphisms need not be separated [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Choose either (a) $\mathcal D_T=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ for one fixed $n\ge1$, with ordinary unbounded derived module operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], or (b) $\mathcal D_T=D(\mathscr S_T)$, where $\mathscr S_T$ consists of module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_T$ and semilinear transition maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$, with componentwise morphisms commuting with transitions. In (b) use the simultaneous ringed-diagram-site operations of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], not completed integral operations or derived maps chosen from their evaluations. Write $P_u\dashv S_u$ for exact inverse image and its total right-derived direct image, and $J_j\dashv P_j$ for exact extension by zero along an open immersion [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Use ordinary derived tensor over the constant ring or over the ring system, respectively.

Let $d_{v,u}:P_uP_v\cong P_{vu}$ be the canonical pullback compositor, $c_{v,u}:S_vS_u\cong S_{vu}$ the inverse of its adjunction conjugate, and $e_{b,j}:J_bJ_j\cong J_{bj}$ the inverse open-adjunction conjugate of $P_jP_b\cong P_{bj}$. These are the canonical derived direct-image and open-extension compositors. They are natural, unital, associative, and identify the canonical adjunction for a composite with the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. If $\mu_u:P_u(F\otimes G)\cong P_uF\otimes P_uG$ is canonical derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], then, after $d$ identifies pullbacks, $\mu_{vu}=\mu_u\circ P_u(\mu_v)$, with the arguments and tensor associators inserted. This assertion also fixes the tensor/composition coherence in setting (b).

For every commutative square
$$Q=\begin{array}{ccc}U&\xrightarrow{k_1}&V\\ r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\ W&\xrightarrow{i}&Z\end{array},\qquad pk_1=ir,$$
with $p,r$ proper and $k_1,i$ quasi-compact open, form $V_W=V\times_ZW$ with projections $b:V_W\to V$, $q:V_W\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The induced $s=(k_1,r):U\to V_W$ is open and closed. Let $\operatorname{pr}_s:F\to J_sP_sF$ be identity on $s(U)$ and zero on its complementary open. Let $\beta:P_pJ_i\cong J_bP_q$ be canonical open base change, normalized by the open unit as in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Define
$$a_Q:P_pJ_i\xrightarrow{\beta}J_bP_q\xrightarrow{J_b\operatorname{pr}_sP_q}J_bJ_sP_sP_q\cong J_{k_1}P_r,$$
and define its proper-adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]
$$\Gamma_Q=S_p(J_{k_1}\varepsilon_r)\circ S_p(a_QS_r)\circ\eta_pJ_iS_r:J_iS_r\longrightarrow S_pJ_{k_1}.$$
This is precisely the normalized proper/open map used in [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate], also in setting (b). No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed.

For vertically stacked squares $Q_1,Q_2$ with left proper edges $r_1,r_2$, right proper edges $p_1,p_2$ and middle open $i_1$, the intrinsic clopen construction for their outer rectangle satisfies
$$\Gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(S_{p_2}\Gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\Gamma_{Q_2}S_{r_1}).$$
For horizontally adjacent squares with top opens $k_1,k_2$, bottom opens $i_1,i_2$ and proper verticals $r,p,q$, it satisfies
$$\Gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(\Gamma_{Q_2}J_{k_1})\circ(J_{i_2}\Gamma_{Q_1}).$$
Insert $c,d,e$ in these equations. Squares with identity verticals or identity horizontals give identity comparisons. The pasted $a_Q$ equals the intrinsic clopen-projection $a_Q$ for the outer square. The identities apply to refinement squares $(k_1,i,r,p)=(j_1,j_2,1,u)$ and to all intermediate squares in refining compatible compactification towers [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. They are identities of natural transformations on the entire stated unbounded categories, with no constructibility, Tor, etale-origin or normalized-system hypothesis. In (b) they hold before restriction of scalars, finite evaluation or total limit. No invertibility of $\Gamma_Q$ on arbitrary inputs is asserted.

proof.text: First fix the comparisons on module sheaves, before deriving. The direct-image section identifications for a composite are induced by the unique fibre-product isomorphism; the two identifications for three maps coincide because their projections coincide. Taking the uniquely adjunction-compatible inverse-image comparison gives the unital, associative pullback compositor. The module comparison is the explicit one in lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit: on local tensors it sends $(m\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $m\otimes c_u(a)b$. Its unit equation identifies it with the adjunction comparison, not merely an isomorphism of functors. Constant coefficient identifications are compatible with composition by lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition. In (b) the same formulas commute with every semilinear transition: restriction and multiplication commute with the ring homomorphisms $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Thus they are actual maps of systems. Apply the exact-functor localization to these maps on complexes to obtain $d$. The simultaneous models of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections identify this construction with the specified system pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites); module lift: sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules); explicit system extension written here

proof.text: For $P_u\dashv S_u$, use the composite unit and counit of def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction. The inverse conjugate of $d$ gives $c:S_vS_u\cong S_{vu}$, carrying these composite units and counits to the canonical ones. For ordinary unbounded derived direct images this is the canonical resolution comparison by lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization; in (b) apply the same exact-left-adjoint argument on the stipulated ringed diagram category, with its adjunctions supplied by lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections. For open maps the comparison between $J_bJ_j$ and $J_{bj}$ is uniquely determined by the right-adjoint comparison $P_jP_b\cong P_{bj}$ and its unit equation, by lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation. This gives $e$ with precisely the asserted normalization. Both parenthesizations for three maps have the same adjunction transpose, since $d$ is associative and the composite Hom bijection is the same three successive bijections. Injectivity of transposition identifies them; the identity case is identical with one identity Hom bijection. This proves naturality, associativity, unitality and compatibility with the composite adjunction for $c,e$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), using derived.tex Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); uniqueness of adjunction comparisons

proof.text: The tensor comparison also respects $d$. The monoidal inverse-image comparisons of lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor give this first over $\mathbf Z$. Passing to relative tensor products gives the same equality: after the coefficient identifications a local tensor $x\otimes y$ is sent by either route to $P_ux\otimes P_uy$, with any intermediate scalar multiplied into the final scalar. This follows directly from the formula for the module compositor in Step 1 and the balancing relation, so the equality holds on the sheaf tensor products. To derive it take K-flat resolutions with flat terms as in lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback. Their successive pullbacks remain K-flat with flat terms, and both comparisons are the maps just checked on their total tensor complexes; localization gives $\mu_{vu}=\mu_u\circ P_u(\mu_v)$ after $d$ and tensor associators. In (b) use K-flat complexes on the ringed diagram site and the simultaneous tensor construction of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections. The scalar formula is already an equality of system chain maps, so localization gives the asserted system equality.

source.place: Tag 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules); relative tensor balancing and K-flat derivation of the inverse-image tensor comparison

proof.text: For a square $Q$, the projection $b:V_W\to V$ is an open immersion by base change of $i$. Under this identification $V_W$ is the open inverse image $p^{-1}(W)$; since $k_1$ is open and factors through $b$, its factor $s$ is open as well. The map $q$ is separated, being a base change of the separated map $p$. Since $qs=r$ is proper, lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated makes $s$ proper. The proper-immersion lemma then makes $s$ closed. Thus $V_W=s(U)\amalg C$ for the complementary open $C$. Notice that only separatedness of $p$ over $Z$ was used, and no separated structure morphism to $k$ was required. Moreover $q$ is of finite type by finite-type base change from $p$, and $V_W\to W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type by composition, using lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change. This verifies the finite-type hypothesis of the clopen-decomposition node used next.

source.place: Tags 0F7B-0F7D: open-immersion case; clopenness is the proper-over-separated and proper-immersion factorization underlying the normalization

proof.text: We shall check the pasting of $a$ on module sheaves. For the disjoint open cover $V_W=s(U)\amalg C$, the module equivalence in lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition identifies $F$ with $(s^*F,F|_C)$ and $s_!G$ with $(G,0)$. Consequently a map $F\to s_!G$ is uniquely determined by its restriction $s^*F\to G$, and the projection $F\to s_!s^*F$ is $(1,0)$. For semilinear systems apply this sheaf equivalence at every $n$. Its explicit product-of-sections inverse commutes with restriction of scalars, so the equivalence and projection commute with all transition maps. A morphism of systems is a compatible family of component maps; hence the same uniqueness follows in the abelian system category. Combining this with full faithfulness of $b_!$, supplied by the open unit normalization, shows that a module or system map $b_!F\to k_{1!}G=b_!s_!G$ is uniquely determined by its restriction to $U$. This is a sheaf/system calculation; it makes no assertion that derived evaluation is faithful.

source.place: Tag 04TS (lemma-mapping-property-glue), specialized to the two disjoint open pieces; elementary extension from the cited module equivalence to semilinear systems

proof.text: Construct the sheaf comparison $a_Q$ by the open base-change isomorphism followed by $(1,0)$ in Step 5 and the open/pullback compositors. Its restriction to $U$ is the identity $r^*M\to r^*M$: the restricted base-change map is the identity under the open units, and so is the projection on the selected component. It is the unique map with this property, since its source is $b_!q^*M$ after open base change and Step 5 applies. All operations in this construction are exact functors, so it gives a chain map on every complex and descends to the unbounded derived categories. The localized open adjunction has the localized unit and counit by lem-sfb-adjunction-localization; therefore the localized open base-change map is exactly the unit-normalized derived $\beta$ of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, not an alternative isomorphism. It follows that the localized $a_Q$ is the intrinsic derived clopen composite in the question. Taking its mate by def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate gives the displayed formula for $\Gamma_Q$. The formula is the same $\alpha,\gamma$ normalization explicitly specified by lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate, in both coefficient settings.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), map normalization; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), proper-adjunction transpose; agent clopen construction in the stated ambient categories

proof.text:
For vertical pasting, label the rows $U_a\xrightarrow{j_a}V_a$ for $a=0,1,2$, with proper maps $r_a:U_{a-1}\to U_a$, $p_a:V_{a-1}\to V_a$ for $a=1,2$. On module sheaves form
$$A=(a_{Q_1}P_{r_2})\circ(P_{p_1}a_{Q_2}):P_{p_1}P_{p_2}J_{j_2}\longrightarrow J_{j_0}P_{r_1}P_{r_2},$$
where here $P,J$ denote underived exact functors. After restricting along $j_0$, the second factor is the pullback by $r_1$ of $P_{j_1}a_{Q_2}=1$, since $p_1j_0=j_1r_1$; the first factor restricts to $1$ by Step 6. Thus $P_{j_0}A=1$. Identify its source by open base change with $b_{\rm out,!}q_{\rm out}^*$ and its target with $b_{\rm out,!}s_{\rm out,!}(r_2r_1)^*$. The clopen uniqueness of Step 5 for the outer square identifies $A$ with its intrinsic $a$. This proves the geometric vertical identity before localization, also for system sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose); explicit clopen-normalization verification for the open case

proof.text:
For horizontal pasting, label the two squares by top opens $k_1:U\to V$, $k_2:V\to T$, bottom opens $i_1:W\to Z$, $i_2:Z\to Y$, and proper maps $r,p,q$. On module sheaves the pasted map is
$$B=(J_{k_2}a_{Q_1})\circ(a_{Q_2}J_{i_1}):P_qJ_{i_2}J_{i_1}\longrightarrow J_{k_2}J_{k_1}P_r.$$
Restrict along $k_2k_1$: the factor $a_{Q_2}J_{i_1}$ becomes the identity on $P_pJ_{i_1}$ after restriction to $V$, and the remaining factor becomes $P_{k_1}a_{Q_1}=1$. Hence the restriction of $B$ is identity. As in Step 7 its source is extension from the outer base-changed bottom open and its target is extension from the selected clopen component. Step 5 identifies it with the intrinsic $a$ of the outer square. The identifications here are precisely $e,d$ fixed in Steps 1-2. This proves the horizontal identity as module and system maps.

source.place: Tag 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal); explicit clopen-normalization verification for the open case

proof.text:
Apply the exact functors termwise to complexes in Steps 7-8. The localization universal property carries these equalities of natural transformations, their compositions and their compositors to equalities on the whole unbounded derived categories. Step 6 identifies the resulting maps with the intrinsic $a_Q$ there. Apply clause 2 of lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting to Step 7, with $L_1=P_{r_2}$, $L_3=P_{r_1}$, $L_2=P_{p_2}$, $L_4=P_{p_1}$, $G=J_{j_2}$, $H=J_{j_1}$, $K=J_{j_0}$. It gives
$$\Gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(S_{p_2}\Gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\Gamma_{Q_2}S_{r_1}).$$
Apply clause 1 of the same node to Step 8, with $L_1=P_r,L_2=P_p,L_3=P_q,G=J_{i_1},G_2=J_{i_2},H=J_{k_1},H_2=J_{k_2}$. It gives
$$\Gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(\Gamma_{Q_2}J_{k_1})\circ(J_{i_2}\Gamma_{Q_1}).$$
The composite adjunctions are those of def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, so inserting $c,d,e$ is justified by Step 2. In (b) these are localizations and adjunction transposes in the system category itself, with the simultaneous models of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections. No equality is inferred from equalities of evaluated derived maps.

proof.text: With identity vertical maps the square has equal horizontal opens, its clopen factor is the identity, and $a_Q$ is the identity on open extension under the units; its proper-adjunction mate is the same identity. With identity horizontal maps the proper maps coincide, $a_Q=1_{P_p}$, and clause 4 of lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting gives $\Gamma_Q=1_{S_p}$. For a refinement $u$ the definition gives $uj_1=j_2$, with proper edges $1,u$ and open edges $j_1,j_2$, so it is among the squares already treated. Every intermediate proper/open square in a compatible refinement tower has precisely the hypotheses used in Steps 4-9, hence the same identities apply. The construction used no constructibility, Tor, boundedness, etale-origin, completed coefficient or cartesian-system condition. It constructs natural transformations on the stated categories, without asserting their invertibility.
